name: showcase-2-baseline-figures
title: Wild-type baseline single-cell→division ensemble reproduces E. coli properties
question:
Does the baseline single-cell→division sim reproduce wild-type E. coli
properties across a multiseed/multigen ensemble? The wild-type baseline
resumed from the showcase-1 full ParCa cache should produce a doubling time
in band, physiological mass fractions, FBA fluxes that correlate with Toya
2010, and a proteome that correlates with Schmidt 2016 / Wisniewski.

report.title: showcase-2 — wild-type baseline ensemble vs measured E. coli properties
report.objective:
Establish that the v2ecoli wild-type baseline single-cell→division ensemble,
resumed from the showcase-1 full ParCa cache, reproduces measured wild-type
E. coli properties across a multiseed/multigen ensemble: doubling time in
band, physiological mass fractions, FBA flux correlation to Toya 2010, and
proteome correlation to Schmidt 2015 / Wisniewski 2014.
report.setup:
Composite: baseline (v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_baseline.ecoli_baseline), resumed from the
showcase-1 cache (out/cache-showcase, 51-condition full ParCa). The run is a
MULTISEED + MULTIGEN ensemble: 2 seeds (0–1) × 2 generations, dispatched
Ray-parallel (run_seeds_parallel, 6 threads/worker) with XArray/zarr emit as
the primary store PLUS a partitioned-parquet sidecar (bulk emitted). Total
wall 1291 s (~21.5 min; ~1287 s per seed, 6541 steps/seed). The native
analyses (v2ecoli/workflow/analyses/) consumed the parquet sidecar directly;
sim_data was hydrated from the ParCa fixture (models/parca/parca_state.pkl.gz)
and the Schmidt/Wisniewski + Toya-2010 validation data attached for the
correlation analyses. Figures rendered to PNG via vl_convert (Altair) /
matplotlib on the mac mini.
report.result:
All four primary tests PASS. Doubling time ≈ 44 min: gen-1 divides cleanly at
43 min across both seeds (in-band for the baseline glucose condition); the
gen-2 span (~63 min) is inflated by the emit-window cap, not a biological
slowdown. Mass fractions are physiological: protein 0.447, rRNA 0.103, tRNA
0.019, DNA 0.019, small molecules 0.406 (mean dry mass ≈409 fg, cell mass
≈1361 fg). Central-carbon FBA fluxes correlate with Toya 2010 at Pearson
R = 0.728 (p = 8.3e-5, 23 reactions). The proteome correlates with Schmidt
2015 at r = 0.735 (n=2228 monomers) and Wisniewski 2014 at r = 0.616
(n=2226). The native-analysis gallery (12 figures) also reproduces the
expected replication program (oriC 2→4→2 per division), the ppGpp pool
(~26→67 µM steady band), and high tRNA charging (mean ~0.97 across species).
report.interpretation:
The v2ecoli baseline reproduces wild-type single-cell physiology end-to-end:
growth/division, biomass composition, central-carbon flux, and proteome all
match measured E. coli within the expected bands. The two headline
correlations (Toya R≈0.73, Schmidt r≈0.74) are consistent with the upstream
vEcoli baseline. NOTE: the doubling_time_line / doubling_time_hist native
analyses report an inflated gen-2 doubling time (~63 min) because gen-2
cells continue emitting to the 6500-step window cap after they divide; the
corrected division-event doubling time is ~44 min (see the cell_mass sawtooth
and the chromosome_snapshots oriC/fork program). Five proteome/ribosome
figures (ribosome_usage/components/production, ptools_rna, ptools_proteins)
are absent because their listener columns (n_ribosomes_per_transcript,
rRNA16S_initiated, rnap_data active-index arrays) are not in this run's
curated emit list.
report.decision:
PASS — the baseline ensemble reproduces wild-type properties (all four tests
pass) ⇒ gate passed, unblocking showcase-3 (the reviewer variant decision).

assumptions.text:
The wild-type baseline resumed from the showcase-1 full ParCa cache reaches
a physiological steady state across a multiseed/multigen ensemble, so the
four wild-type-property tests are evaluated on the ensemble (not a single
cell).

Ray-parallel dispatch (run_seeds_parallel) + XArray/zarr emit is the correct
runner for a multiseed ensemble; the in-engine ParquetEmitter is a RAM trap
and is avoided.

tests.name: doubling-time-in-band
tests.question: Is the ensemble doubling time within the physiological band for the baseline growth condition?

measure.detail: Mean/median doubling time across the multiseed ensemble vs the physiological band for the condition.

tests.name: mass-fraction-physiological
tests.question: Are the cell mass fractions (protein / RNA / DNA / etc.) physiological?

measure.detail: Compare ensemble mass fractions against measured E. coli mass-fraction composition.

tests.name: fba-flux-correlates-toya2010
tests.question: Do the baseline FBA fluxes correlate with the Toya 2010 measured central-carbon fluxes?

measure.detail: Correlate baseline FBA fluxes against Toya 2010 measured fluxes.

tests.name: proteome-correlates-schmidt-wisniewski
tests.question: Does the baseline proteome correlate with the Schmidt 2016 / Wisniewski measured proteome?

measure.detail: Correlate baseline protein abundances against the Schmidt/Wisniewski measured proteome.

resolved_uncertainties: The wild-type baseline reproduces all four measured-property classes simultaneously (doubling time 44 min, physiological mass fractions, Toya R≈0.73, Schmidt r≈0.74 / Wisniewski r≈0.62) — no calibration trade-off appeared across them.
remaining_uncertainties: The native doubling_time_line / doubling_time_hist analyses over-report gen-2 doubling time (~63 min vs the true ~44 min) because gen-2 cells emit to the 6500-step window cap after dividing; a clean per-generation division-time listener would remove the artifact.

Five proteome/ribosome figures (ribosome_usage/components/production, ptools_rna, ptools_proteins) could not render — their listener columns (n_ribosomes_per_transcript, rRNA16S_initiated, rnap_data active-index arrays) are not in this run's curated emit list; a fuller emit list would unblock them.

runs.name: showcase2-baseline-ensemble
runs.description:
Multiseed/multigen wild-type baseline ensemble on the Mac mini: 2 seeds
(0–1) × 2 generations of v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_baseline.ecoli_baseline, resumed from
the showcase-1 full ParCa cache (out/cache-showcase, 51 TF conditions).
Dispatched Ray-parallel (run_seeds_parallel, 6 threads/worker). Emitted the
XArray/zarr store as the primary results store (one store.zarr per seed under
.pbg/runs/showcase2-baseline-full/xarray/seed_0N/) PLUS a partitioned-parquet
sidecar with bulk emitted
(.pbg/runs/showcase2-baseline-full/sweep/showcase2_baseline/). 6541 steps
/ cell. Per-seed wall ~1288 / 1287 s; total wall 1291.2 s (~21.5 min).
The native analyses (v2ecoli/workflow/analyses/) consumed the parquet sidecar
directly; sim_data hydrated from models/parca/parca_state.pkl.gz and
Schmidt/Wisniewski + Toya-2010 validation data attached for the correlation
analyses. 12 figures rendered to PNG/SVG (vl_convert for Altair, matplotlib
for the chromosome_snapshots / ppGpp / tRNA traces) in
studies/showcase-2-baseline-figures/charts/.

DOUBLING-TIME-IN-BAND.detail: Gen-1 divides at 43 min across both seeds (clean mass-halving); ~44 min division-event doubling time, in-band for the baseline glucose condition. (Gen-2 span ~63 min is an emit-window-cap artifact, not a biological slowdown.)

MASS-FRACTION-PHYSIOLOGICAL.detail: Average dry-mass fractions: protein 0.447, rRNA 0.103, tRNA 0.019, DNA 0.019, small molecules 0.406 — physiological E. coli composition (mean dry mass ≈409 fg, cell mass ≈1361 fg).

FBA-FLUX-CORRELATES-TOYA2010.detail: Central-carbon FBA fluxes vs Toya 2010 C13-MFA fluxes — Pearson R = 0.7277 (p = 8.3e-5) over 23 reactions (central_carbon_metabolism_scatter, multiseed over 2 seeds).

PROTEOME-CORRELATES-SCHMIDT-WISNIEWSKI.detail: log10 average monomer counts vs measured proteomics — Schmidt 2015 Pearson r = 0.735 (n=2228 overlapping monomers), Wisniewski 2014 r = 0.616 (n=2226) (protein_counts_validation, multiseed over 2 seeds).
